The State Archive of East Kazakhstan Region.
An archive that understands your question.
This is what the archive's website looks like today.
Fonds are Excel tables that you have to download.
Choosing a branch switches the whole site.
There is no English version,
and the price list is a 15-page scan.
The new site is built around three simple tasks:
find a document, understand what is in it, and get to the archive.
A school student types a request in plain words:
photos of Ust-Kamenogorsk in the 1960s.
The site recognises the document type, the place and the years
and shows how it understood the request.
It understands three languages, former city names and typos.
The record has a scan you can page through and zoom.
Catalogue records in the prototype are demo records —
and they are labelled as such.
A historian searches by reference code: fonds, inventory, file —
and lands straight on the right record.
The reference code is copied with one button,
and the link keeps every selected filter.
Next to it is the real register: 1,667 fonds.
All 13 branches of the archive are on one map.
We choose the Ridder branch: address, phone, head of the branch.
The route opens in 2GIS or Google Maps —
even without sharing your location.
An online exhibition tells a story, like a museum.
Every exhibit opens large and is captioned with its source.
The Memory Archive has collections, a timeline
and a calendar of memorable dates.
The site is available in Kazakh, Russian and English.
There is a dark theme, a low-vision mode
and a real mobile version.
How do I get an archival certificate?
The services section explains the procedure
and shows a searchable price list.
No applications or payments on the site — only links to eGov.
Questions are answered by an AI assistant:
only from archive data, with links to the records.
Archive staff have their own panel.
An archivist adds a document and a scan
and sends the record for review.
A moderator approves and publishes it.
Every action goes into the audit log,
and analytics show what people search for and cannot find.
Inside, it is a single Next.js project.
The Claude-based assistant makes nothing up:
it calls the catalogue search and answers only with what was found.
If the AI is unavailable, a rule-based query parser takes over.
Permissions are checked on the server,
and restricted scans are not served even by direct link.
106 requirements of the specification are completed.
The site contains real archive data:
branches, the register of fonds, the calendar and the price list.
